name: Reproducible Notebooks and Pipelines
title: Reproducible Notebooks and Pipelines
answer: Reproducible notebooks and pipelines are the practice of capturing every step of a quantitative analysis, from raw data ingestion to final figure or model output, in a form that another researcher can rerun with the same results. This includes computational notebooks such as Jupyter, scripted workflows, and containerised pipeline definitions. The scope covers version control of code and data, dependency pinning, and documentation of parameter choices. It sits within the broader effort to make AI research claims checkable against the original paper rather than a secondary search tool.

sections.body: Reproducible notebooks and pipelines are the practice of capturing every step of a quantitative analysis, from raw data ingestion to final figure or model output, in a form that another researcher can rerun with the same results. This includes computational notebooks such as Jupyter, scripted workflows, and containerised pipeline definitions. The scope covers version control of code and data, dependency pinning, and documentation of parameter choices. It sits within the broader effort to make AI research claims checkable against the original paper rather than a secondary search tool.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on a combination of local development machines, shared compute clusters, and cloud environments. Notebooks typically execute in a browser or IDE against a Python or R kernel, while pipelines are orchestrated by tools such as Snakemake, Airflow, or GitHub Actions. Reproducibility depends on pinned package environments, often captured in files like requirements.txt, environment.yml, or Docker images. Data and intermediate artifacts are stored in versioned object storage or data registries.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done by writing code in small, linear cells or pipeline stages that each produce an auditable intermediate output. Researchers record the exact software versions, random seeds, and data splits used for every run. Notebooks are often paired with a script or parameterised pipeline so that a full run can be executed end to end without manual cell-by-cell interaction. Outputs are compared against saved expected results or checksums to catch silent changes.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk centre on data provenance, licensing of code and datasets, and the risk of unreported manual edits. A notebook that runs on one machine may fail on another if dependencies or data paths are not pinned, so teams often require a clean-room rerun before a result is accepted. Access controls and audit logs track who changed a pipeline and when. The site's practice of linking to the original paper rather than a search tool supports checking claims against primary sources.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward self-contained executable research objects that bundle code, data, environment, and narrative in one artifact. More pipelines will use declarative specifications and automatic dependency resolution to reduce drift. Expect tighter integration between notebooks and model registries so that a published figure can be traced back to the exact model version and training run. Reproducibility checks may become a standard part of peer review and internal model validation.
